hints: Look first at the high wavenumber end above 3000, a broad dip there tells you a lot about O-H groups.
Notice the very strong, sharp dip at about 1700, this is the classic position for a C=O stretch.
Combine the presence of C=O with the absence of any broad O-H to decide which functional group family must be present.
walkthrough:
**Check for O-H above 3000**

Look at 3200 to 3600. There is no broad absorption there, just a flat baseline. That rules out an alcohol O-H and a carboxylic acid O-H.

Rule: $O-H$ (alcohol) = broad peak 3200 to 3600, $O-H$ (acid) = very broad 2500 to 3300

**Identify the strong carbonyl peak**

There is a very strong, sharp dip at about 1700. This is characteristic of C=O stretching.

Rule: $$C=O \text{ stretch } \approx 1680 \text{ to } 1750 \text{ cm}^{-1}$$

**Check the C-H region**

There are sharp dips just below 3000. These are C-H stretches from alkyl groups, as expected for a small organic molecule.

Rule: $$C-H \text{ stretch } \approx 2850 \text{ to } 3100 \text{ cm}^{-1}$$

**Match to the options**

We need a molecule with C=O and C-H but with no O-H. That is a ketone or an aldehyde, not an acid or an alcohol. Only $\text{CH}_3\text{COCH}_3$ fits perfectly.

options.A: Incorrect. CH3CH2CO2H is a carboxylic acid. It would show C=O near 1700 but also a very broad O-H absorption from 2500 to 3300. The spectrum has a flat baseline there, so this cannot be the compound.
options.B: Incorrect. CH3CH(OH)CH3 is propan-2-ol, a secondary alcohol. It would show a broad O-H peak at 3200 to 3600 and no C=O peak at 1700. The spectrum shows the opposite, strong C=O and no broad O-H.
options.C: Correct. CH3COCH3 is propanone, a ketone. It has C-H bonds giving peaks just below 3000 and a strong C=O peak at about 1700, with no O-H absorption. This matches the observed spectrum exactly.
options.D: Incorrect. CH3COCH2OH is a hydroxy ketone. It would show both C=O near 1700 and a broad alcohol O-H at 3200 to 3600. The absence of the broad O-H peak rules it out.
